name: AP22804AW5-7
title: AP22804 / AP22814: single-channel current-limited load switch, 2.7 V to 5.5 V, 50 mΩ, 2.5 A or 3.0 A
summary: A one-channel high-side power switch for USB ports and other hot-plugged rails, with a 50 mΩ N-channel switch running from 2.7 V to 5.5 V. The AP22804 is rated for 2.5 A and the AP22814 for 3.0 A of continuous output; both limit overload and short-circuit current, shut down when hot, block reverse current, ramp the output softly, discharge the output when off and report faults on an open-drain FLG pin after a 6 ms blanking time. The A versions enable on a high EN, the B versions on a low EN. AP22804AW5-7 is the 2.5 A, active-high part in SOT25, 3000 to a reel.
key_figures: 50 mΩ typ, 65 mΩ max at VIN = 5 V, IOUT = 1 A
80 µA typ enabled; 0.1 µA typ shut down

notes: Order code AP228X4 E PP-R: X is 0 for the 2.5 A AP22804 or 1 for the 3.0 A AP22814; E is A (EN active high) or B (EN active low); PP is M8 (MSOP-8), W5 (SOT25) or SN (U-DFN2020-6); R is -7 or -13, the tape-and-reel suffix.

SOT25 and U-DFN2020-6 parts carry a two-letter identification code then year (Y, 0 to 9), week (W: A to Z for weeks 1 to 26, a to z for weeks 27 to 52, z also for week 53) and a code letter. MSOP-8 parts carry the logo, the part number AP228X4X and a YWX line of year, week and internal code.
Further features listed for the family: UL recognition under file E322375, IEC60950-1 CB scheme certification, lead-free, RoHS compliant, halogen and antimony free.

circuits.title: Typical application, enable active high
circuits.description: The switch sits between a 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply and a load. A 1 µF capacitor decouples IN; OUT carries a 0.1 µF ceramic and a 120 µF polarised bulk capacitor. A 10 kΩ resistor from the supply pulls up the open-drain FLG line, which leaves the circuit as a fault signal. EN is driven by an on/off control line, high for on with an A part.

where.RDS(ON): switch on-resistance at the highest ambient

operation.text: IN takes a 1 µF X5R or X7R ceramic to GND, placed close to the part; a further 10 µF or 47 µF at the input helps when output load steps are large, cutting supply ringing. For hot-plug use OUT takes at least 100 µF of low-ESR electrolytic or tantalum capacitance, or 10 µF of MLCC, and always a 0.1 µF ceramic, which makes the part more immune to short-circuit transients. The bulk capacitance limits output droop when a device is hot-plugged and, during a hard short, limits the negative swing caused by stray inductance. Without bypassing, a short at the output can ring the input above its absolute maximum, and even a brief overshoot can destroy the control circuitry.
EN switches the output and takes GPIO levels: a high of 1.5 V or more turns the switch on, a low of 0.65 V or less turns it off. EN must not float. Hold EN low while power is applied or removed.

The output ramps under internal control. Turn-on delay tD(ON) runs from EN crossing 50 % to VOUT reaching 10 %; rise time tR is VOUT going from 10 % to 90 %. Turn-off delay tD(OFF) runs from EN crossing 50 % to VOUT falling to 90 %; fall time tF is VOUT going from 90 % to 10 %. The same definitions hold for active-low B parts and active-high A parts, with EN inverted.

The switch stays off until IN reaches about 2 V, even with EN asserted, and turns off quickly if IN falls below about 2 V, which suits hot-insertion systems where the switch cannot be turned off before input power goes away. Threshold 1.6 V to 2.4 V rising, 180 mV hysteresis.

Current is measured with a sense FET, which adds no series resistance. In overload the part holds the output current constant and lets the output voltage fall; it shuts down completely only when the fault lasts long enough for thermal limiting to act. Three cases: an output already shorted when the part is enabled or powered is clamped at once to a safe current; a short or overload arriving while enabled can draw a brief higher current before the limit responds, after which current is held at ILIMIT or ISHORT; a load rising slowly past the rated current is allowed up to the current-limit threshold, which the part survives, and is then held at ILIMIT. Recovery from over-current, short circuit and over-temperature is automatic.

A sensor watches junction temperature. Near +140 °C, as in a sustained overload or short, the switch turns off; it turns on again after cooling by about +35 °C, and keeps cycling so until the fault or the input power is removed.

FLG is open drain. An over-current or a thermal shutdown pulls it low after a nominal 6 ms deglitch, and it stays low until both conditions clear. A brief over-current, such as charging a large capacitive load, does not assert FLG because of the deglitch, so no external filter is needed against false reports.

When the part is disabled, an internal path of about 90 Ω (130 Ω max) discharges the output capacitor, removing residual output voltage when no load or output resistor is present. With 1 µF on the output it takes about 0.4 ms to fall below 0.5 V from 5 V.

If VOUT rises above VIN by 50 mV (25 mV to 75 mV) for 6 ms, the switch turns off; it turns on again once the reverse condition is gone. Reverse current is limited to about 400 mA at VOUT - VIN = 100 mV.

Put the 1 µF input capacitor and the 0.1 µF plus 100 µF output capacitors right at the pins to keep parasitic inductance low. Keep traces short, make input and output traces wide, and use a ground plane to carry heat away. On U-DFN2020-6, connect the exposed pad to GND.
